> systems onto their own VLANs over that link, `node2` on VLAN 10 and `node3` on

> still reach each other.

## Trial `vlan-segmentation-rhel7__XcTB8tS`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 as 802.1Q sub-interfaces over the shared eth1 link, configured node1 (VyOS) to route between the two VLANs with IP forwarding enabled and no blocking firewall, and directly verified bidirectional cross-VLAN reachability (ttl=63 confirming the routed hop) while preserving each node's independent internet egress via eth0. All configuration was made persistent (VyOS config.boot save; RHEL ifcfg/route files) and this persistence, plus full functional recovery, was directly demonstrated across sequential reboots of all three nodes with matching boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.880 | 0.920 | 41/11 (+12 dropped) |

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.880**. One transient, self-corrected misconfiguration occurred: the first ifcfg-eth1.10/eth1.20 attempts on node2/node3 (cmd-f5055db0f8774b62, cmd-9f2d885e675443fd) included a GATEWAY= line that installed a competing zero-metric default route via the VLAN sub-interface, which would have hijacked internet-bound traffic away from eth0. This was recognized and immediately corrected in the very next commands (cmd-641db4f69e6e465d, cmd-6d584624e4644ca4), which rewrote the ifcfg files without GATEWAY and added scoped route-eth1.NN files instead; the final verified route tables show only the intended single default route via eth0 plus the specific peer-VLAN route, so no residue remained. Two earlier unprivileged attempts to write ifcfg files (cmd-8866bbb1337f40cc, cmd-2e614d40178440ec) failed with permission denied and made no state changes. The lifecycle diff for node1 confirms package-health (dpkg), no new failed services, and no unexplained residue beyond expected reboot artifacts (new systemd-private tmp dirs, reboot.log) on all three nodes.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-8866bbb1337f40cc`, `cmd-2e614d40178440ec`, `cmd-f5055db0f8774b62`, `cmd-9f2d885e675443fd`, `cmd-641db4f69e6e465d`, `cmd-6d584624e4644ca4`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`

- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.880); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
